meta.title: The End of Harness Engineering
meta.subtitle: the loop writes the harness, the human writes the exam
meta.author: Reading notes on a 2026 paper by a team of Chinese researchers
meta.kicker: Reading notes · The End of Harness Engineering (2026)
meta.abstract: A harness is the program written around a model, and writing it by hand has been the skill. The paper argues that this is ending. A hand-written harness is one guess about one task on one afternoon; once it ships, it runs for months, unread and unscored. In the loop the paper describes, the harness is a file that grades itself: a small 4B model reads what failed and proposes 8 edits, and only the edit that scores best on held-out questions survives. This repeats every round. The big model stays frozen; only the file around it changes.

blocks.markdown: Harness engineering has meant writing the program around the model by hand. A person studies one task, writes one file, and ships it. After that nobody reads the file and nobody scores it, so a wrong guess keeps running for months. The paper's answer is to stop writing that file by hand and let a loop write it, with the model itself untouched.

Each round starts from what failed. A small 4B model reads the failures and proposes 8 edits to the harness file. Every edit is scored on held-out questions, the best one is kept as the next version, and the other seven are dropped. The big model is never retrained: it stays frozen while the file around it changes.

blocks.caption: Two ways to write a harness. The hand-written path is a single guess; the loop-written path reads failures, proposes edits, and keeps only what survives held-out scoring.

lines.text: Input: harness h_0, frozen model M, scoring set Q
F := failures of M running h_n on the task set
E := 8 edits proposed by the 4B editor from F
for each e in E: s(e) := score of e on Q
h_{n+1} := h_n + the e with the highest s(e)

blocks.markdown: Three parties touch the system and only one of them is a person. The human writes the scoring set: the questions the harness is graded on. The 4B model writes every edit to the harness file. The big model writes nothing; it is the same frozen model in every round, and only the file around it changes.

blocks.caption: Who writes what in the loop
Held-out score by round. Each round the editor proposes eight edits; the seven rejected are grey, the kept one is orange. The harness changes only when an edit wins.

blocks.markdown: When a loop writes the harness, frameworks become disposable and the exam becomes the job. The order of work flips: first the questions the harness will be graded on, then the code. That inversion is the paper's real claim, and it is a governance claim as much as an engineering one, because the scoring set is the artifact a human still owns.

blocks.title: Takeaway
blocks.body: Write the exam before the code.

items: One guess about one task on one afternoon.
4B: a model of about four billion parameters, small next to the frozen model it edits for.
Held-out questions are kept out of the editing step and used only for scoring.
